newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN RESERVE BANK HINTS AT RATE CUT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN RESERVE BANK HINTS AT RATE CUT.

text.p: South Africa's central Reserve Bank has hinted that a cut in interest rates may take place soon, Business Times reported on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted Reserve Bank deputy governor Chris de Swardt as saying the bank was beginning to see scope for a rate cut from the current Bank rate of 17 percent.
De Swardt said the bank "is beginning to see scope for a decline in interest rates, although we are still looking at the timetable".
De Swardt said the bank had officially reduced its economic growth forecast for 1997 to 2 percent from 2.5 percent, mainly on reduced agricultural output.
Financial markets have been rife with speculation of an imminent rate cut.
A swathe of local economic data is due to be released next week, all of which should continue to point the way to a lowering of the Bank rate.

Money supply growth, private sector credit extension growth and consumer inflation are all expected to have fallen in June, adding further ammunition to economists' call for at least a one percentage point fall by the end of the year.
De Swardt said the increases in money supply and credit extension had been flat for two months while inflation declined to 9.5 percent in May.
He said he was encouraged by the relatively small outflows of capital since a partial lifting of exchange controls on individuals on July 1.
"While the daily outflows are picking up slightly, only 100 million rand has been effected to date. We expect total outflows of no more than 130 million rand in July".

He said a number of factors, including the effect of the weak gold price on the rand and uncertainty about the future impact of the exchange control easing, still inhibited the easing of monetary policy.
